sample_size.notes: Mixed R/C profile — NOT a pure reversal pattern. Often continuation of the prior decline.

three_phases.name: event_decline
three_phases.description: Sharp price drop on news/event (earnings miss, guidance cut, sector shock).

three_phases.name: bounce
three_phases.description: Short-lived rebound as shorts cover and dip buyers enter. Typically 1-7 trading days.

three_phases.name: postbounce_decline
three_phases.description: Resume decline — usually exceeds the bounce and continues lower for weeks/months.

target_calculation.description: Target = bounce high - (event decline height). Project downward from the bounce peak.
target_calculation.notes: This is NOT the same as classic chart pattern measure rule. DCB target depends on the EVENT magnitude, not pattern geometry.

failure_definition.description: DCB has NO traditional break-even failure rate. Failure is defined as: postbounce decline does NOT make a new low below event_low. Quantify as pct of cases where postbounce decline < bounce high.

lookahead_phases.notes: Two distinct lookahead windows — pipeline must track them separately.

performance_statistics.reliability_note: Bounce is temporary; treat as SHORT signal opportunity, not long.

notes: PDF source: Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed.), chapter 54, p852-887 (36 pages — large chapter).
CRITICAL: Dead Cat Bounce is EVENT-DRIVEN, not a price-formation pattern. It CANNOT use the same measure rule / failure framework as classical chart patterns (head & shoulders, triple tops, etc.).
Legacy digitized folder has NO file dead_cat_bounce_digitized.json — detector uses temporal lookahead=120 as placeholder. This file is the FIRST spec for DCB.
Pipeline MUST track 3 phases separately: event → bounce (1-7d) → postbounce decline (~6mo). Using a single lookahead_bars value is INCORRECT.
Bulkowski provides 7 statistical tables (54.2 through 54.8) — reproducer should extract all for full picture.
